correctness.rationale: The centered counts and the frequencies assigned to those counts are correct. The Finding first correctly defines the covariance as Δ_q/q³, but then asserts in its frequency paragraph that the nonzero values −1, 2q, and −q are covariances. They are centered counts; the covariances are −1/q³, 2/q², and −1/q². For example over F₇ every nonzero-slope shift has covariance −1/343, not −1. The same error is in the slogan. For the underlying count, each nonsquarefree cubic determines a unique repeated root r, and two repeated roots r and s for the two translates must differ because a nonzero affine shift cannot have a double root. Write f=(T−r)²(T−s+b) and d=s−r. Vanishing of the value and derivative at s determines b=−h(s)/d² and gives d³=2h(s)−ud=u(s+r)+2v, with a unique inverse for every solution. For odd q, (d,s+r) are independent coordinates: a nonzero slope gives q−1 solutions, and a constant shift gives q times the number of cube roots of 2v. For even q the equation becomes d²=u with d≠0, giving q solutions for u nonzero and none otherwise. This covers characteristic three too. Both marginal nonsquarefree counts are q², so Δ_q is the joint nonsquarefree count minus q. Direct independent cubic-discriminant enumeration of every shift for q=2,3,5,7,13 agreed with the centered-count formulas (replay: /workspace/branches/independent-checks/record4.py); the frozen verifier was read but not executed and tests counts, not the mislabelled covariance. Correcting the numerical labels alone leaves the originality and value failures below, so no repair is delivered.

evidence: For all nonzero affine h, the prior d=0 case cannot occur because h and h′ have no common root. Substituting h(x)=ux+v into the prior equation gives d³+d u−2ux−2v=0. For odd q and u≠0, each d≠0 determines x; for u=0 it is the cube equation d³=2v with x free. In characteristic two the very same two original equations leave d²=u with x free, since 2d(x−s)=0. The prior value equation determines the residual root uniquely, and its inclusion–exclusion uses precisely the two q²-element nonsquarefree loci.
